Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Insurance Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Instructions for queuing up can be found by pressing the star key followed by one on your touchtone phone. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Insurance Holdings' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Underwriting Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Operating Officer; and Mark Patel, Chief Claims Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Insurance Holdings' performance for Q3. We delivered strong results, driven by robust investment income yields, the effectiveness of our reinsurance program, favorable expense ratio trends, positive changes in actuarial assumptions, the impact of strategic pricing changes on premium volume, solid reinsurance recoveries, and a well-balanced asset allocation. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation initiatives.

David, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

David Thompson: Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $485 million, or $1.92 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included higher investment yields, efficient reinsurance recoveries, expense discipline, and assumption updates that supported reserve releases. Our combined ratio was 92.3%. Investment income for the quarter was $1.55 billion. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with risk-based capital at 520%. Our expense ratio also improved to 26.8%.

Let me dive deeper into some of these core elements starting with our investment income yield, a critical metric for us calculated as annualized net investment income divided by average invested assets. It reflects the return on our portfolio, funded by our insurance float of $145 billion at quarter-end, up 8% year-over-year. This yield directly boosts our operating ROE, which was 14.2% this quarter, helping offset underwriting volatility in our P&C and group life segments.

In Q3, our investment income yield reached 4.35%, up 55 basis points from 3.80% in the prior-year quarter and 12 basis points from Q2's 4.23%. Year-to-date, we're at 4.28%, on track for the top of our 4.1% to 4.4% full-year guidance. This is our strongest quarterly yield since late 2007, placing us at the 85th percentile among public P&C peers like Travelers, Chubb, and Progressive, according to Morningstar. The industry average was around 3.9%, per NAIC data, dragged by life insurers' long-duration books.

The higher-for-longer rate environment is the main tailwind, with the 10-year Treasury averaging 4.42%, up from 3.85% last year. We're reinvesting maturities at higher coupons, with new money yield at 5.12%, up 28 basis points sequentially, into investment-grade corporates at 5.4% to 5.8% and agency MBS at 5.2
